properties.name: Advice
properties.location: Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge
properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge.

Minor Flooding occurring along the Kiewa at Bandiana and likely at Kiewa from Sunday Afternoon

Moderate to heavy rainfall observed across the Kiewa River catchment since Friday evening caused river level rises and areas of minor flooding. No further significant rainfall is forecast for the next few days.

The Kiewa River Channel at Kiewa is currently at 3.26 m and rising, below the minor flood level. The Kiewa River Channel at Kiewa is likely to exceed the minor flood level (3.30 m) Sunday afternoon. The river may peak near 3.40 m during Monday, with minor flooding. 
The Kiewa River at Bandiana is currently at 2.95 m and steady, with minor flooding. The Kiewa River at Bandiana is likely to remain above the minor flood level (2.80 m) though to Monday afternoon. Further rises are possible as upstream flows arrive but expected to remain below the moderate flood level (3.10 m).
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
Impacts in your area: 
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 07/09/2026 01:00 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app
  • Facebook
  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.
Accessibility: 
The following services can help you, or someone you know, access information during an emergency. 
  • To access this information in other languages, call the Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450 (freecall) and ask them to call VicEmergency Hotline. 
  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.

properties.name: Watch & Act
properties.location: Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham
properties.webBody:
This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham.

NEAR MODERATE FLOODING OCCURRING AT BARHAM

Upstream flows from the Murray River, combined with flood waters from the Goulburn River, are causing near moderate flooding along the Murray River at Barham where the river level is peaking. River levels are likely to remain above the minor flood level through to early next week as flood waters continue to arrive from upstream.

Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham:
  • Near moderate flooding is occurring at Barham.
  • The Murray River at Barham is currently at 5.72 m and steady, peaking near the moderate flood level (5.80 m). The Murray River at Barham is expected to remain around 5.80 m over the weekend. The river is likely to remain above the minor flood level (5.50 m) into early next week.
Stay safe - avoid the flooded area. Be aware of potential hazards caused by flooding and never enter floodwater.
What you should do:
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
  • Rising floodwater can be dangerous. Be aware of water levels rising near you.
  • Monitor weather forecasts and river levels. 
  • If you are camping close to a creek or river, you may be at risk of flooding and need to move to higher ground, away from waterways.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
  • Go to www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/(https://www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/) 
  • For emergency assistance, call SES on telephone number 132 500. In life-threatening emergencies, call 000 (triple zero) immediately.


Impacts in your area:
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
  • Camping grounds may be flooded.
  • Boating in floodwaters is dangerous due to debris, submerged trees and other hidden dangers.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 07/09/2026 01:30 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app

  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.
Accessibility:

  • To access this information in other languages, call the Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450 (freecall) and ask them to call VicEmergency Hotline.
  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.
